# 1\. LAB OVERVIEW

## 1.1  Why This Lab Exists

Observability platforms bill by volume: spans, log gigabytes and active metric series. A single new label can multiply the series count, and keeping every trace costs more than most teams expect. Good governance measures first, cuts the right thing and keeps the evidence needed during incidents.

In this lab you price one month of the shop's telemetry from a usage file, find the label that exploded the metric series, run a head-versus-tail sampling simulation on 10,000 traces, calculate the cost of an optimised plan and write the recommendation.

| 🎯  NIIT iRUN Alignment |
| :---- |
| INCIDENT OWNERSHIP: You can explain why a telemetry bill grew and which single change fixes most of it. |
| TROUBLESHOOTING EXCELLENCE: You keep errors and slow traces while dropping the bulk of normal data. |
| OPERATIONAL READINESS: You never optimise without a measured before and after. |

## 1.2  Lab Scenario

| 📢  Incident Briefing — The Telemetry Bill Doubled |
| :---- |
| TIME: 14:00 │ PRIORITY: MEDIUM │ ASSIGNED TO: You |
| REQUEST RECEIVED: "The observability bill is much higher since the catalog 2.4 release. Finance wants a plan that cuts the cost without losing what we need during incidents." |
| CONTEXT: The usage file lists monthly volumes and unit prices for traces, logs and metrics. series.txt is a sample of the metric series after the release (a new label endpoint was added). traces-sample.csv holds 10,000 traces with an error flag and a slow flag. |
| YOUR MISSION: Price the baseline, find the driver, compare sampling methods, calculate an optimised plan and recommend it. You have 28 minutes for the core tasks. |

*Figure: Day 6 Lab 3 — Starting Environment: Terminal in lab3-cost-governance; usage.csv, series.txt, traces-sample.csv, cardinality.py and sample\_sim.py*

## 1.3  Conceptual Foundation

Cost \= volume × unit price. The three signals have different cost drivers: traces by number of spans, logs by gigabytes ingested, metrics by number of distinct series.

*Figure: Cost Levers — Traces: Tail Sampling · Logs: Drop INFO but Count It · Metrics: Remove the High-Cardinality Label*

| Signal | Cost Driver | Lever | What You Give Up |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Traces | Spans per month | Tail sampling: keep errors, slow traces and a small share of the rest | Most normal traces |
| Logs | GB per month | Drop INFO lines, keep WARN/ERROR; keep a counter metric | INFO detail in incidents |
| Metrics | Active series | Remove or fix the label with unbounded values | Per-ID breakdown |

## 1.4  Learning Objectives

• Calculate the monthly cost per signal from volumes and unit prices

• Find a high-cardinality label and count the series one value creates

• Explain why histograms multiply cardinality

• Compare head sampling and tail sampling by the errors they keep

• Calculate the cost and saving of an optimisation plan

• Write a recommendation that names the levers, the numbers and what is kept for incidents

## 1.5  What You Will NOT Do

| 🚫  Hard Stops — Absolute Prohibitions for This Lab |
| :---- |
| DO NOT edit usage.csv or the other data files. |
| DO NOT optimise by dropping everything — errors and slow traces must stay. |
| DO NOT use real credentials or any live platform; this lab needs none. |
| DO NOT round before the final answer; round only the numbers you write down. |

# 3\. CONCEPT DEEP-DIVE BEFORE STARTING

## 3.1  Measure Before You Optimise

Optimise only after you know where the money goes. A before-and-after number proves the saving and shows what was lost. Cost per signal \= monthly volume ÷ unit size × price per unit.

| 💡  Why This Matters Operationally |
| :---- |
| A saving without a measurement is a guess. Finance and on-call both need the numbers: how much was saved and which evidence is still there during an incident. |

## 3.2  The Critical Distinction: Head Sampling vs Tail Sampling

**Head sampling** decides at the start of a trace (keep 10 % at random): cheap, but it throws away errors blindly. **Tail sampling** decides after the trace is complete: keep all errors and slow traces plus a share of the rest. It needs a collector that holds traces for a short time, but it keeps the evidence.

| ⚠️  Most Common Mistake With Sampling |
| :---- |
| Using head sampling and assuming the errors are still there. At 10 % you keep only about one error in ten. |

## 3.3  Cardinality

Each distinct combination of label values is one series. A label with unbounded values (an ID in a URL) creates new series without limit, and a histogram creates one series per bucket plus a sum and a count for every value.

# 4\. LAB TASKS

*Figure: Day 6 Lab 3 — Four-Task Workflow: Price → Cardinality → Sampling → Recommendation*

| TASK 1 — PRICE: Monthly Cost per Signal |
| :---- |

| 1 | Calculate the baseline cost | ⏱ 7 min |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

Open data/usage.csv. For each row: monthly cost \= monthly\_volume ÷ unit\_size × price\_per\_unit\_usd. Add the rows per signal.

| ⌨  Task 1 — Calculate |
| :---- |
|  |
| cat data/usage.csv |
| \# traces: 51,840,000 spans / 1,000,000 x 1.80 |
| \# logs: 12 GB x 0.50 \+ 1.5 GB x 0.50 |
| \# metrics: (3,000 \+ 7,000) series / 1,000 x 0.80 ![][image7] |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| traces 93.31 · logs 6.75 · metrics 8.00 · total 108.06 USD per month |
| **1.A Record the cost per signal and the total. Which signal is the biggest driver and was your pre-lab guess right?**  Answer: Traces 93.31, logs 6.75, metrics 8.00; total 108.06 USD per month. Traces are the biggest driver (86 % of the bill). |
| **1.B Of the metrics cost, how much comes from the new endpoint label?**  Answer: 7,000 extra series ÷ 1,000 × 0.80 \= 5.60 USD, which is 70 % of the metrics cost. |

| TASK 2 — CARDINALITY: Find the Label That Exploded |
| :---- |

| 2 | Count distinct label values and series per value | ⏱ 7 min |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| ⌨  Task 2 — Cardinality |
| :---- |
|  |
| python3 [cardinality.py](http://cardinality.py) ![][image8] |
| grep \-c 'endpoint="/api/products/1"' data/series.txt ![][image9] |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| series in file: 7000 |
| endpoint distinct values: 500 · le: 12 · service: 1 · route: 1 |
| series created by ONE endpoint value (/api/products/1): 14 |
| 14 |
| **2.A Which label caused the explosion, how many series does one product ID create and why does a histogram make it worse?**  Answer: The endpoint label (500 distinct values). One ID creates 14 series: 12 histogram buckets plus the sum and the count. 500 × 14 \= 7,000 series. |
| **2.B The label looks like the route /api/products/:id with the ID filled in. How do you fix it at the source, and why is a drop at scrape time only containment?**  Answer: Fix at the source: record the route template (/api/products/:id) instead of the concrete URL. A scrape-time drop stops the storage cost but the exporter still produces the data, the instrumentation stays wrong and the next label can explode again. |

| TASK 3 — SAMPLING: Head 10 % vs Tail |
| :---- |

| 3 | Run the sampling simulation | ⏱ 7 min |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| ⌨  Task 3 — Sampling |
| :---- |
|  |
| python3 sample\_sim.py ![][image10] |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| traces 10000 \| errors 254 \| slow 401 |
| HEAD 10%  kept 1041 (10.4%)  errors kept 24 of 254  slow kept 45 of 401 |
| TAIL      kept 1582 (15.8%)  errors kept 254 of 254  slow kept 401 of 401 |
| **3.A How many errors does each method keep and what share of all traces is stored?**  Answer:  Head 10 % keeps 24 of 254 errors (about 9 %) and stores 10.4 % of all traces (1,041 of 10,000). Tail sampling keeps all 254 of 254 errors (100 %) and all 401 slow traces, storing 15.8 % of all traces (1,582 of 10,000).  |
| **3.B Why can tail sampling decide on errors but head sampling cannot?**  Answer:  An error is only known after a request finishes; head sampling makes its keep/drop decision at the start of the trace before the outcome exists, whereas tail sampling buffers the spans and decides after the complete trace finishes.  |

| TASK 4 — RECOMMENDATION: Optimised Cost and Saving |
| :---- |

| 4 | Calculate the optimised plan and write the recommendation | ⏱ 7 min |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

Plan: traces use tail sampling (kept share from Task 3), logs keep only WARN and ERROR, metrics drop the endpoint label (base series only).

| ⌨  Task 4 — Calculate |
| :---- |
|  |
| \# traces: baseline x tail kept share |
| \# logs: only the WARN+ERROR row |
| \# metrics: only the base series row |
| \# saving % \= (baseline \- optimised) / baseline x 100 ![][image11] |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| traces 14.76 · logs 0.75 · metrics 2.40 · optimised total 17.91 USD · saving 83.4 % |
| **4.A Record the optimised cost per signal, the total and the saving.**  Answer: Traces `14.76 USD`, logs `0.75 USD`, metrics `2.40 USD`; optimised total is `17.91 USD/month`, saving `83.4 %` against the `108.06 USD` baseline.  |
| **4.B Why does a counter of INFO lines stay correct although the INFO lines are not stored?**  Answer: The log-to-metric counter increments in the collector pipeline before the `INFO` log text is dropped, so every `INFO` event is counted accurately while only the raw text payload is discarded.  |
| **4.C Write the recommendation (at least four levers with numbers and what you keep for incidents).**  Answer: 1\) **Tail-sample traces** (`−78.55 USD/mo`, `93.31 → 14.76 USD`): keep `100 %` of errors (`254/254`), `100 %` of slow traces (`401/401`), and `10 %` of normal traces. 2\) **Drop INFO logs with a log-to-metric counter** (`−6.00 USD/mo`, `6.75 → 0.75 USD`): retain `WARN`/`ERROR` logs plus an `INFO` volume counter. 3\) **Remove the high-cardinality `endpoint` label** (`−5.60 USD/mo`, `8.00 → 2.40 USD`, eliminating `7,000` series) and fix instrumentation at the source to emit the route template (`/api/products/:id`). 4\) **Tiered retention**: retain change events (`30` days) and `WARN`/`ERROR` logs (`14` days) longer than any remaining `INFO` data (`3` days). Total spend drops from `108.06 USD` to `17.91 USD/month` (`−83.4 %`) while preserving full incident triage signal.  |

# 6\. TROUBLESHOOTING — COMMON ISSUES & FIXES

| Issue / Error | Cause | Diagnosis | Fix |

| python3: command not found | Python missing | python3 \--version | Use python on Windows; install 3.8+ |
| Cost differs by cents | Rounding or wrong unit size | check unit\_size column | Spans are priced per million |
| sample\_sim numbers differ | Edited traces-sample.csv | re-copy the folder | The simulation is seeded; numbers must match |
| Cardinality shows 1 value | Wrong file | ls data | Run from lab3-cost-governance |

# 7\. INSTRUCTOR DEBRIEF — 7 MINUTES

## 7.1  Discussion Questions

| Discussion 1 — Measure First |
| :---- |
| Why did the plan start with a price list and not with a sampling rate? |
| What would you tell finance about the saving? |
| Key insight: A measured before-and-after is the proof of the saving and of what was lost. |

| Discussion 2 — What You Keep |
| :---- |
| Which data do you still have during an incident? |
| Which data did you give up? |
| Key insight: Errors, slow traces, WARN/ERROR logs and the INFO counter stay; bulk normal data goes. |

## 7.2  Common Mistakes — Learn From These

| Mistake | Why It Happens | Consequence | Prevention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Cutting before measuring | Pressure to save | Wrong cut | Price each signal first |
| Head sampling for errors | It is the default | Errors lost | Tail sampling |
| Scrape-time drop only | Quick fix | Instrumentation stays wrong | Fix the label at the source |
| Dropping INFO without a counter | Forgetting the rate | No volume metric | Log-to-metric before the drop |
